โรงเจในสวน หรือศาลเจ้าเซ้งเหล่งเก้ง ปราก: Rong Jae Nai Suan or Seng Leng Keng Shrine appears in Thetsaban Mueang Takua Pa (Takua Pa Town Municipality) documents as an ancient shrine over a century old, but the same document does not provide the year construction began, so it cannot be pinpointed to a specific reign.
ผู้ก่อตั้งที่เอกสารเทศบาลระบุคือ นายส้อ: The founder identified by municipal documents is Mr. So Thian Seng, an overseas Chinese. Upon completion of the shrine, the deity Qingshui Zushi, or Chao Pho Yat Namkhang, was invited from China to be enshrined. The place likely served as both a place of worship and a spiritual center for the Chinese community in the mining and port town of Takua Pa. However, the year of construction, the founder's policy reasons, and its daily role in that era lack site-specific evidence.
เอกสารท้องถิ่นอีกชุดเล่าว่านายส้อเส็งเคย: Another set of local documents mentions that Mr. So Seng had worked with Ku Chai Tueng Shrine before opening the shrine in the garden. However, it cannot be verified if this is the same person as Mr. So Thian Seng, so they are not presented as the same fact.
ไม่พบปีหรือเหตุการณ์ที่ยืนยันได้: No verified year or event found
จากแหล่งที่ตรวจสอบได้ ยังไม่พบหลักฐานว่า: From verifiable sources, no evidence has been found regarding when the shrine changed hands, was abandoned, or was restored. There is also no specific evidence on how the 2004 (B.E. 2547) tsunami affected this building.
ยังไม่พบรายการขึ้นทะเบียนโบราณสถานของโรง: No historical site registration record for Rong Jae Nai Suan has been found, nor is there information that it was ever converted for other business or public building uses. The only verified information during the transition period is the continuity of the place name and memories of the old shrine. The history of other shrines in the old town area should not be borrowed to fill the gaps.
บริบทเมืองตะกั่วป่าเปลี่ยนจากเมืองเหมือง: The context of Takua Pa transformed from a mining and maritime trade town into a historical and cultural town, but the sources found do not yet connect city-level changes to specific events at Rong Jae Nai Suan.
ปัจจุบันแหล่งข้อมูลออนไลน์ที่ตรวจสอบได้ย: Currently, verifiable online sources do not confirm who the caretaker is, whether the shrine is open daily, the condition of the building, or if any restoration projects are underway. Therefore, it should not be described as open as a tourist attraction or accessible without an appointment.
หลักฐานร่วมสมัยที่พบคือบทความรีวิวซึ่งรา: A contemporary piece of evidence found is a review article reporting the sale of Ko Sui snacks at Rong Jae Nai Suan during the Vegetarian Festival. This information shows that the place is still used as a community activity spot during the festival. However, this is a report from a blog, not a schedule announcement from the shrine, and it does not verify that the activity is still held every year.
สำหรับผู้เดินทาง ควรใช้ที่อยู่ระดับซอยโร: For travelers, the address at the level of Soi Rong Phra, Thanon Rat Bamrung should be used as a starting point, and it should be verified with locals or the municipality before traveling, as there are no verified coordinates, opening hours, phone numbers, or official contact channels yet.

องค์เทพที่เทศบาลระบุว่าประดิษฐานในศาลเจ้: The deity that the municipality notes is enshrined in the shrine is also known as Chao Pho Yat Namkhang, with a history of being invited from China. ก่อนมีอาคารถาวร โรงเรียนเต้าหมิงเปิดสอนภ: Before having a permanent building, Tao Ming School unofficially taught Chinese by private individuals. When the Private Schools Act of 1918 (B.E. 2461) took effect, the school formally requested establishment in 1920 (B.E. 2463) using the name 'Toh Beng' in the Hokkien dialect, before changing to the Mandarin 'Tao Ming'. This word conceptually means guiding to knowledge.
อาคารที่ยังเห็นอยู่สร้างขึ้นใน พ.ศ. 2465: The building still seen today was constructed in 1922 (B.E. 2465) with funds raised from mining tycoons and Chinese merchants in the old market, Yan Yao area, as well as merchant networks from Ranong and Phuket. Another official source describes it as the work of the Chinese Merchants Association involved in tin mining, to allow Chinese descendants to learn the Chinese language. The applied Sino-Portuguese building with a zinc roof is therefore not just a school, but evidence that wealth from mining, trade, and Chinese networks was transforming into community institutions.
ในเวลานั้นตะกั่วป่าเป็นย่านการค้าและขนส่: At that time, Takua Pa was a trade and transport district tied to the river and sea. The town grew from tin ore, with Chinese from Fujian (Hokkien), Guangdong, and Hainan arriving as laborers, merchants, and entrepreneurs. The school served to enrich the linguistic and cultural roots of the Chinese community in the prosperous mining town.
แหล่งข้อมูลท้องถิ่นระบุว่าเหมืองแร่ตะกั่: Local sources indicate that Takua Pa tin mines gradually closed down starting in the 1970s (B.E. 2520s), causing the town's liveliness to decline, while Tao Ming School subsequently ceased operations. Verifiable official sources only confirm that 'the school has been dissolved' and the building is under the care of the Tao Ming School Foundation, Takua Pa, but do not specify the year of closure or details of the handover.
ยังไม่พบหลักฐานอ่านได้ที่ยืนยันว่าอาคารไ: No readable evidence has been found to confirm whether the building was directly affected by the 2004 (B.E. 2547) tsunami or if any restoration occurred in a specific year. Thus, it should not be concluded that it was damaged or repaired from that event, even though the Takua Pa area has places related to tsunami disaster management and the old town has revived its role in cultural tourism.
เอกสารขอบเขตเมืองเก่าของ ONEP ระบุแนวเขต: The ONEP (Office of Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning) old town boundary document indicates a line passing through Tao Ming School, and the Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn Anthropology Centre community database classifies the building among key evidence of the old town. However, this search has not yet found a Krom Sinlapakon (Fine Arts Department) announcement directly specifying the registration of the 'Tao Ming School Building', so the conservation status of the district is separated from the registration status of the building.
